extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, paired with annotated long and short answers from Wikipedia pages.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.citeAs: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 7, pp. 453–466, 2019. https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl_a00276
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are sampled from real anonymized, aggregated queries of 8 words or more issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time. Queries are filtered using heuristics, run through the search engine, and kept if a Wikipedia page is in the top 5 results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Passive Data Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries are filtered using simple heuristics based on length, starting words, and parts of speech to discard non-questions. Questions are then run through Google search, and only those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results are retained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators are presented with a question and a Wikipedia page. They perform three stages: 1) Question Identification (determine if the question is fact-seeking), 2) Long Answer Identification (select the earliest HTML bounding box containing enough information to infer the answer, or mark 'no answer'), and 3) Short Answer Identification (select the entity/entities within the long answer that answer the question, or flag yes/no/no short answer).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was evaluated post hoc by four experts who provided consensus judgments (Correct, Correct but debatable, Wrong). Human variability and disagreement were also analyzed using a subset of 302 examples with 25-way annotations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 annotation per item for training data; 5 annotations per item for development and test data; 25 annotations per item for a 302-example analysis subset.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset relies exclusively on Wikipedia as the source of factual information, which the authors note may introduce biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset excludes shorter queries (under 8 words), 'how to' questions, and domains/sources of factual information other than Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development (validation), and testing of open-domain question answering (QA) and natural language understanding (NLU) systems.
